title: Warp-bubble wall shape and exotic-matter Pareto frontier
objective: Investigate a controlled family of smooth warp-bubble wall profiles and characterize the tradeoff among peak negative energy density, an integrated negative-energy proxy, wall thickness, and bubble radius. Do not assume that one profile family or discretization is representative: generate competing shape hypotheses, search for numerical or convention artifacts, and determine which trends remain stable under at least one independent formulation or implementation.
success_definition: A useful result identifies a reproducible Pareto structure or demonstrates why the proposed structure is not robust. It must distinguish physical or geometric trends from sampling, normalization, boundary, and package-convention effects.
deliverables: A machine-readable comparison of at least two materially different smooth wall-profile families.
A Pareto or tradeoff analysis with sensitivity to resolution and parameter bounds.
At least one attempted falsification of the leading trend.
Explicit assumptions, conventions, failure modes, and a reproducible validator.
preferred_validators: independent SymPy, NumPy, or Wolfram check
resources: Optional pyWarpFactory package, resolved through ASTRA_PYWARPFACTORY_ROOT
Optional warpbubble optimization package, resolved through ASTRA_WARPBUBBLE_OPT_ROOT
Optional GR_python package, resolved through ASTRA_GR_PYTHON_ROOT
linear_control_directions: Define a baseline smooth top-hat wall profile and parameter ranges.
Compute a peak negative-energy proxy over the baseline parameter grid.
Compute an integrated negative-energy proxy over the same grid.
Repeat the grid with a second smooth profile family.
Estimate sensitivity to normalization and integration bounds.
Extract nondominated parameter choices for the measured objectives.
Summarize the observed tradeoffs and limitations.

expert_anchors.goal_advancement: Extent to which the work actually characterizes or falsifies a robust multi-objective tradeoff rather than reporting isolated values.
expert_anchors.hypothesis_quality: Quality and discriminating power of competing profile, scaling, and artifact hypotheses.
expert_anchors.research_depth: Whether later sweeps and checks are motivated by earlier failures, ambiguities, or emerging structure.
expert_anchors.evidence_quality: Resolution studies, independent formulations, convention audits, reachable failures, and numerical stability.
expert_anchors.self_correction: Ability to detect a misleading optimum, normalization issue, boundary artifact, or unstable conclusion and redirect productively.
expert_anchors.cross_perspective_uptake: Causal use of an alternative model's profile family, invariant, falsification, or computational strategy.
expert_anchors.novelty_utility: Whether the frontier or negative result would guide a subsequent scientific or engineering study.
expert_anchors.artifact_reproducibility: Completeness of parameter ranges, package versions, scripts, outputs, and oracle metadata.
